text: The space-bandwidth product caps the neuron count, which scales as lambda^-2. Roughly how many independent neurons does a 6 cm aperture (NA = 0.4) hold at 0.4 THz versus at 500 nm?
choices: About 10^6 at both, independent of wavelength
About 9e9 at 0.4 THz vs about 4e3 at 500 nm (terahertz holds more)
About 4e3 at 0.4 THz vs about 9e9 at 500 nm, because capacity grows as lambda^-2
explanation: Because diffraction forbids pixels finer than about lambda/(2*NA), the independent-neuron count ~(2A*NA/lambda)^2 scales as lambda^-2; the same 6 cm aperture holds ~4e3 neurons at 0.4 THz but ~9e9 at 500 nm. Option 1 reverses the scaling (shorter wavelength holds more), and options 0 and 2 wrongly make capacity wavelength-independent (40,000 is the Lin 2018 per-layer pixel count, not the SBP cap).
